definition: Memory for GPT, a system that teaches language models how to manage their own memory hierarchy, creating the illusion of infinite context size for longer-running agent sessions.
details: Memory for GPT, a system that teaches language models how to manage their own memory hierarchy, creating the illusion of infinite context size for longer-running agent sessions.

explainer.lead: Memory for GPT: a system that teaches language models to manage their own memory hierarchy. It creates the illusion of infinite context size for longer-running agent sessions.

tiers.eli5: The model keeps its own notebook, writing things down and looking them up so it doesn't forget what happened earlier.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for long-running agent sessions where a fixed context window is too small, letting the model manage its own memory hierarchy.
tiers.paperLevel: A system that teaches language models to manage their own memory hierarchy, creating the illusion of infinite context size for longer-running agent sessions.

explainer.example: An agent in a long session moves older information into its managed memory and retrieves it later instead of holding it all in context.
